user: How do card payments differ from SEPA transfers?
answer:
| | Card payment | SEPA transfer |
|---|---|---|
| Flat fee | EUR 0.00 | EUR 0.35 |
| Percentage fee | 1.2% of the EUR equivalent | 0% |
| Counts toward transfer limits | Yes | Yes (settled outgoing transfers) |

For example, a EUR 100 card payment costs EUR 1.20 in fees (1.2% of EUR 100, no flat fee). A EUR 100 SEPA transfer costs EUR 0.35.

I should also correct my earlier answer: card payments count toward the same daily and monthly limits as transfers, so your EUR 5,000 daily limit applies to card spending too.

fragments.text:
Fee details
## Card payment fee
Card payments carry a percentage fee on the EUR equivalent. No flat fee
applies.

Fee details
## Fees and limits
Fees charged by Verta do not count towards the transfer limits of the customer.

Verta tariff schedule
## Transfer fees by type
| Transfer type | Flat fee | Percentage fee |
|---|---|---|
| Internal | EUR 0.00 | 0% |
| SEPA | EUR 0.35 | 0% |
| SWIFT | EUR 15.00 | 0.3% |
| Card payment | EUR 0.00 | 1.2% |

The percentage fee is calculated on the EUR equivalent of the transfer amount.

Limit operations
## What counts towards a limit
Only settled outgoing transfers count towards the daily and monthly transfer
limits. Card payments count. Incoming transfers, internal transfers between the
own accounts of one customer, and fees charged by Verta do not count.
